title: Transient drive open/close logic
approved_scope: Create a proof-only runtime factory that derives a run-scoped Expo cache URI from a generated validated runId and passes it unchanged as the sole Bare worklet argument.
Add the versioned OPEN_CLOSE_TRANSIENT_DRIVE command that opens an empty Corestore/Hyperdrive drive, closes it with drive.close(), and returns the exact two-field capability receipt.
Modify only the five source/test paths named in the approved card plus P1.A1b evidence and status artifacts.
excluded_scope: Hyperswarm, discovery, replication, product P2PService APIs, persistence, cleanup/janitor logic, direct bare-fs dependency, filesystem-path logging/RPC/receipts, iOS, commits, pushes, deployment, and external writes.
acceptance: HP-A1: a valid generated runId creates new Directory(Paths.cache, dubbridge-p2p, proofs, runId).uri; the sole URI reaches Bare.argv[0], and OPEN_CLOSE_TRANSIENT_DRIVE returns exactly { capability: transient-hyperdrive-corestore, schema_version: 1 } after drive.close().
EC-A1b: invalid runId or missing/non-file URI returns redacted PROOF_STORAGE_CONFIG_INVALID before Corestore/Hyperdrive creation or any network activity.
Focused Jest, npm run check:bare-worklet, typecheck, lint, three Reflection passes, phase-2 review, coverage certification, owner verification, and status synchronization pass.
constraints: The URI is host-derived and only startup data: never an RPC field, receipt, log, or product API parameter.
Corestore/Hyperdrive own storage access; do not add direct bare-fs dependency. Normal close is drive.close(); store.close() is only for failure before a drive exists.
No storage handle or network behavior occurs on invalid bootstrap configuration.
Stop and return to scoring/review/approval if any edit or behavior escapes the frozen P1.A1b boundary.
